key_insight: A polymorphic high-entropy oxide photocatalyst paired with microalgae as a sacrificial scavenger can substantially boost solar-driven CO2 conversion to CO and CH4.
engineering_relevance: This work suggests a scalable route to improve photocatalytic carbon capture and conversion by combining materials design for charge/CO2 handling with a sustainable biological co-reactant.
method: Designed AB2O6-type HEO (Cs1/7Ba4/7Bi2/7)(Nb1/2Ta1/2)2O6 with layered perovskite + pyrochlore bi-polymorphy.
Used Cs/Ba to raise surface basicity for CO2 adsorption, Bi to promote polarization/charge separation, and Nb/Ta to support charge transport.
Compared photocatalytic performance with no sacrificial agent, microplastics, and microalgae.
evidence_signal: With microalgae present, CO and CH4 production increased by about 10× and 4×, respectively, relative to the HEO-only system, indicating strong catalytic enhancement.
watch_item: The approach depends on integrating and managing living biomass during photocatalysis, so stability, reproducibility, and process control may limit practical deployment.
paper_title: Sustainable photocatalytic CO2 conversion using microalgae as a carbon-negative scavenger
